text: Build job 3, part 1, of the records-history plan (docs/design/records-history.md sections 5.2, 5.3, 6.1 and 10, decision D111): athena land --pr writes a landing-intent record (PR number, head sha, head tree, expected base, job ids) to the athena/records branch before it asks the host to merge, and a landing record (PR number, head sha, the commit the host made, merge method, the pull request's commits with their trees and the job and verification covering each, and the intent it fulfils) after the merge, in a records-branch commit that takes the pull request's head as an extra parent so its commits stay reachable. Use the record types in athena-data history.rs and the writer in athena-git records_branch.rs, and push the records branch to the remote. Everything land does today (trailers, records under records/, the rebuild of the work branch) stays as it is. Tests with the fake host: a landing writes both records in order with the right fields; the landing commit's second parent is the PR head; a merge the host refuses leaves an intent and no landing record.
